results.title: Nomad eSIM - Review 2024 - PCMag Middle East
results.content:
(Credit: Nomad/PCMag)

In the US, Nomad offers six regular plans: 1GB for $4.50 (seven days), 1GB for $6 (seven days), 3GB for $11 (30 days), 5GB for $14 (30 days), 10GB for $24 (30 days), and 20GB for $35 (30 days). Though they offer the same 1GB of data, the $4.50 and $6.00 plans are indeed different. The $4.50 plan supports AT&T and T-Mobile and starts automatically when connected to a network or after a 30-day window. The $6.00 plan is limited to just AT&T but provides a more flexible 60-day activation window.

Nomad also offers shorter day plans ranging from 1 to 10 days that come with 1GB of high-speed data per day plus unlimited data throttled to 512Kbps. The website and app clearly outline each plan’s details, and all listed prices include applicable taxes.

(Credit: Nomad/PCMag) [...] (Credit: Nomad/PCMag)

Nomad's US pricing is in line with other data-only service providers like Airalo and Saily, which charge $4.50 and $4.39, respectively, for 1GB of data over 7 days.

To use Nomad's eSIM service, your device needs to be unlocked and eSIM compatible. Many modern phones, such as the Apple iPhone 16 and the Samsung Galaxy S24, support eSIMs. If you are unsure if your device will work with Nomad, the company lists the phones, tablets, and laptops that are compatible with its service. [...] (Credit: Iyaz Akhtar)

You can view your data usage in the Manage tab of the Nomad app, where you can also see details like when your plan will expire and buy more data. If your data is running low or is set to expire, you will receive a notification. You can purchase additional data at the same price as regular plans. For example, an additional 1GB costs $4.50.

results.title: eSIM Price Comparison 2026: Cheapest Plans, Price per GB & Best Value Providers
results.content:
|  |  |  |  |  |
    ---  --- 
   | Region | Typical Data Plan | Validity | Average Price | Approx. Price per GB |
   | Europe | 10GB | 30 days | ~$15–$25 | ~$1.5–$2.5 |
   | Asia | 10GB | 30 days | ~$12–$22 | ~$1.2–$2.2 |
   | Global (multi-region) | 10GB | 30 days | ~$35–$60 | ~$3.5–$6 |

   ### 🏰Europe eSIM price overview

   Europe is one of the most competitive regions for travel eSIM plans. Many providers offer regional packages covering multiple EU countries.

   Key characteristics include:

    Wide multi-country coverage
    Many plans support 30–40 European destinations in one package. Moderate price per GB
    Most plans average around $1.5–$2.5 per GB depending on the provider. Convenient for multi-country travel [...] Travelers can move between countries without switching SIM cards. If you plan to visit several countries in one trip, regional plans can be easier to manage. You can also compare this option with traditional SIM cards in our guide on Travel eSIM vs Tourist SIM Card.

   ### 🌏Asia eSIM price overview

   Asia often offers some of the most affordable travel eSIM plans. Many destinations have competitive mobile networks and lower data costs.

   Typical characteristics include:

    Lower average pricing
    Many plans cost around $12–$22 for 10GB. Strong coverage in popular destinations
    Countries such as Japan, Thailand, and South Korea usually provide stable 4G or 5G networks. Flexible options for short trips [...] However, compatibility can still vary depending on several factors:

    The exact phone model
    The regional version of the device
    Whether the phone is carrier-locked or unlocked

   Before purchasing an eSIM plan, it’s recommended to check a device compatibility guide to make sure your phone supports eSIM installation.

results.title: Ubigi eSIM review 2026: Plans, pricing and features
results.content:
Written by Julio Osuna

Updated: February 27, 2026

Ubigi is an eSIM provider offering data plans across 200+ destinations with options ranging from one-off purchases to annual subscriptions. Pricing starts at $2.90, with plans covering everything from 500MB single-day options to unlimited data packages. However, coverage availability and customer support limitations vary depending on your destination and travel needs.

In our Ubigi eSIM review, we’ll discuss all these features, as well as network coverage, data speeds, and some alternatives so that travelers can make a proper choice before their trip. We’ll also look at Holafly, a top eSIM with unlimited data to consider for your next trip.

An eSIM you can rely on [...] #### Europe

| Data limit | Price | Duration |
 --- 
| 500 MB | $ 2 | 2 days |
| 3 GB (Europe extended) | $19 | 15 days |
| 3 GB | $7 | 30 days |
| 10 GB | $12 | 7 days |
| 10 GB | $16 | 30 days |
| 50 GB | $59 | 30 days |
| Unlimited | $26 | 7 days |
| Unlimited | $44 | 15 days |

### Customer service and technical support

Ubigi offers customer support through multiple channels. Users can access support through their online contact form available on the Ubigi website, which requires details like your name, email, eSIM number, device type, and the nature of your request.

Saily positions itself as a privacy-focused eSIM provider with both fixed and unlimited data plans for Mexico. Setup happens through the app, and you land connected without manual activation.

Install through the Saily app, choose your Mexico plan, and your connection activates when you arrive.

This can be frustrating when you're trying to make a fixed data plan last through your trip.

Saily doesn't offer a free trial, so you're committing before testing the service.

Privacy-conscious travelers willing to test without a trial, those who value having both fixed and unlimited plan options, travelers primarily staying in major Mexican cities.

Overall I do believe that the value derived from a Sim Local plan is higher than that of other eSIM providers that I’ve used in the past. [...] You’re supposed to be able to check your usage by dialing #123#, but for some reason that wasn’t working for me. I could have reached out to them on WhatsApp to get clarification while on my trip, but I never got around to it, so it wasn’t too big of a deal to me.

Alternatively, I just looked at my cellular settings on my phone to see how much data I had used, so this was a good enough checkpoint for me.

## How does Sim Local compare to other eSIM providers?

The Sim Local Asia regional plan that I used offered 20GB of data along with 50 SMS and 15 minutes of calling for $35 USD.

For a comparable data package size, Ubigi offers a 25GB data plan for 30 days in Asia for $44 USD. This is more expensive compared to Sim Local and does not come with SMS and voice. [...] Pricepoint-wise it’s actually cheaper than other providers, but with the additional SMS and voice capabilities, it gave me more peace of mind when traveling that I could be contacted by anyone who needed to reach me while I was out of the country. And it came in handy in helping me coordinate logistics from one country to the other.

And if you really don’t need calls or SMS they have cheaper data-only plans which would perform similarly to other data-only eSIM providers.

## Who is a Sim Local eSIM best for?

In my opinion, Sim Local offers data plans that are great for everyone whether you’re traveling solo or with a small or large group.

results.content:
A 20GB data package for 30 days from Airalo is closer in price to Sim Local at $39 USD, but also doesn’t come with SMS and voice.

I’ve provided the data plan content details in the table below for easy comparison. (Please note all prices here are as of March 2026)

| Provider | Duration | Data | Cost | SMS | Voice Minutes |
 ---  ---  --- |
| Sim Local | 31 days | 20GB | $35 USD | 50 | 15 |
| Ubigi | 30 days | 25GB | $44 USD | 0 | 0 |
| Airalo | 30 days | 20GB | $39 USD | 0 | 0 |
| Verizon | 31 days | Unlimited | $372 USD (for 31 days) | Unlimited | Unlimited |

Overall I do believe that the value derived from a Sim Local plan is higher than that of other eSIM providers that I’ve used in the past. [...] You’re supposed to be able to check your usage by dialing #123#, but for some reason that wasn’t working for me. I could have reached out to them on WhatsApp to get clarification while on my trip, but I never got around to it, so it wasn’t too big of a deal to me.

Alternatively, I just looked at my cellular settings on my phone to see how much data I had used, so this was a good enough checkpoint for me.

## How does Sim Local compare to other eSIM providers?

The Sim Local Asia regional plan that I used offered 20GB of data along with 50 SMS and 15 minutes of calling for $35 USD.

For a comparable data package size, Ubigi offers a 25GB data plan for 30 days in Asia for $44 USD. This is more expensive compared to Sim Local and does not come with SMS and voice. [...] Pricepoint-wise it’s actually cheaper than other providers, but with the additional SMS and voice capabilities, it gave me more peace of mind when traveling that I could be contacted by anyone who needed to reach me while I was out of the country. And it came in handy in helping me coordinate logistics from one country to the other.

And if you really don’t need calls or SMS they have cheaper data-only plans which would perform similarly to other data-only eSIM providers.

## Who is a Sim Local eSIM best for?

In my opinion, Sim Local offers data plans that are great for everyone whether you’re traveling solo or with a small or large group.

I went full-on ADHD hyper focus mode for like 100 hours creating this detailed spreadsheet to help you compare/contrast several eSIM companies. Prices, discounts, perks, refund policies, support, device compatibility… the whole deal. [...] What sets it apart: ETravelSim is one of the few options that offers calling with some packages. This means you’ll get a local phone number with your plan. I’ll admit this is rarely a necessity, however I’ve now had a couple situations where I needed to make a phone call to a landline when all I had was an eSIM with data.

Pros: They have some great regional packages for places you’re likely to country hop, like Southeast Asia, Europe, and Africa (on special for $27/30 days as of August 2025). It’s also great that you can hotspot with most plans. It’s definitely the best eSIM for call and text abroad. Also, ETravelSim offer the most competitive discount at 15% off for first time users. [...] ## Choosing the best eSIM for you

While all eSIMs are more convenient than traditional SIM cards, they’re not all made equal and you’ll have to do some digging to choose the best eSIM for your needs and travel style. (And you’re already here researching it, so that’s half the battle!) Here are some key factors to consider:

 Pricing. Is it affordable?
 Ease of Use. Will it be easy to purchase, install, and activate?
 Customer support. Will someone be available to help you if you run into issues?
 Compatibility. Does it work with your phone model?
